newsitem.title: USA: Whittman clarifies use of shelf shares.
newsitem.headline: Whittman clarifies use of shelf shares.

text.p: Whittman-Hart Inc said late Tuesday that the bulk of its common share shelf registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission would not be sold on financial markets.
Whittman-Hart Inc filed the shelf registration earlier Tuesday with the SEC for up to 4,066,400 common shares.
Of the total, 66,400 shares will be offered for sale by Edward V. Szofer (or his donees), The Chicago, Ill., based company said.

"The four million shares are to position us for use from time to time for potential acquisitions and will not be sold in the financial markets." said David P. Shelow, General Counsel of Whittman-Hart, in a statement late Tuesday.
Whittman-Hart provides strategic information technology services designed to improve its clients' productivity and competitive position.

Later, a spokesman for Whittman-Hart said the 66,400 Szofer shares were only registered for possible later resale as a result of the conversion of the company to a "C" corporation from an "S" corporation prior to going public May 3, 1996.
